To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the brain's working memory system is composed of a network of brain regions that encode and maintain information in a flexible manner, and that the prefrontal cortex controls the activity of this network.
working memory is a distributed network of brain areas that represent mnemonic content and control the allocation of cognitive resources.
working memory is supported by distributed neural networks that include regions that are also engaged when processing information in nonworking-memory contexts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural basis of working memory in humans, and with how this memory is controlled and regulated by prefrontal circuits.
the neural mechanisms underlying working memory and their role in cognitive control.
how information is maintained in working memory and how it is used to guide behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

working memory is not a single unitary system, but rather a complex network of brain regions, each of which contributes a unique set of functions to the maintenance of information over a short delay period.
the PFC is a critical node in a distributed neural circuitry that controls working memory, but that this circuitry is not limited to the PFC.

working memory is a flexible and adaptive system that allows us to temporarily represent information in a context dependent manner, and to use this information to guide behavior in a goal-directed manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PFC, in conjunction with the striatum, is the seat of executive control, which is the ability to flexibly adapt behavior in response to changes in the environment.

the brain's working memory system has a modular organization, with different brain regions encoding different types of information, and a hierarchical organization, with the PFC exerting top-down control over lower level mnemonic representations.
working memory is the product of a dynamic interplay of multiple brain regions, and that this interplay can be understood by a combination of behavioral and brain imaging methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
working memory is not a single, unitary process.
the neural basis of working memory is not a single, unitary process, but instead reflects a complex interaction between multiple brain regions, including sensory cortex and PFC.
a cognitive neuroscience of working and long term memory can help us understand how the brain coordinates the flow of information across the brain, and how it uses this information to guide behavior.
